field.classification: Bronchodilators, sympathomimetic, short acting beta-2 adrenergic agonist
field.action: Selective beta-2 adrenergic agonist that causes bronchial smooth muscle relaxation. In the case of hyperkalemia, Albuterol assists in the reuptake of potassium into the cells from the bloodstream.
field.indications: Treatment of bronchospasm in patients with reversible obstructive airway conditions (wheezing in COPD/Asthma/Anaphylaxis); treatment of inhaled airway/respiratory irritant agents; hyperkalemia induced bronchospasms; crush injury.
field.adverse: Tachycardia, dysrhythmias, palpitations, hypertension, chest pain, tremors, dizziness, nervousness, headache, nausea/vomiting, dry mouth.; Dose: Unit dose plastic vial containing 2.5mg/3ml.
field.precautions: May precipitate angina and dysrhythmias. Albuterol can effect vision in young children/infants, so use with caution in children <20kg.

doses.label: Bronchospams (wheezing); crush injury
doses.dose: Patients weighing >20kg: 2.5mg in 3cc saline (one pillow) nebulized with 8 L/min O2. May repeat as needed. Patients weighing <20kg: Use half of one pillow (1.25mg)

field.action: Blocks sodium, potassium, and calcium channels; prolongs the action potential’s duration and delays repolarization; decreases AV conduction and SA node function.
field.indications: V-Fib and Pulseless V-Tach refractory to defibrillation. Stable, pulsing Ventricular Tachycardia
field.contraindications: hypersensitivity to amio or to iodine (iodine is used in amio’s chemical structure), cardiogenic shock, bradycardia, AV blocks
field.adverse: Hypotension, heart failure, worsening dysrythmias, prolonged QT interval, bradycardia, AV block, dizziness, fatigue, cough, progressive dyspnea, nausea, vomiting.
field.precautions: May produce vasodilation and hypotension. May have negative inotropic effects. May prolong QT interval.

doses.label: Pulseless VF/VT
doses.dose: 300mg IV/IO push, followed by 150 mg IV/IO push in 3-5 minutes for refractory VF/VT

doses.label: Wide complex tachycardia (stable)
doses.dose: 150 mg slow IV/IO push or drip over 10 minutes

doses.label: Pulseless VF/VT
doses.dose: 5mg/kg IV/IO bolus to a maximum single dose of 300mg, May repeat dose twice to an overall maximum of 450mg administered.

doses.label: Perfusing VT
doses.dose: 5mg/kg IV/IO over 20-60min (max of 300mg)

field.action: Prevents thromboxane A2 formation, which causes platelets to clump together (aggregate). Has antipyretic and analgesic properties.
field.indications: New onset of chest pain with suspected cardiac origin (for antiplatelet, not for pain relief)
field.contraindications: Hypersensitivity to drug, bleeding disorders including active GI bleeds.
field.adverse: GI bleeding, epigastric distress, nausea, vomiting, heart burn. Aspirin will increase bleeding time.
field.supplied: Supplied as baby aspirin, chewable, 81 mg each.
field.notes: Give prior to NTG dose for chest pain/AMI patients. OK to administer to patients who have already taken daily dose of ASA. As stated above, not for pain relief, DO NOT ask if their chest pain improved after administering.

doses.label: Suspected cardiac related chest discomfort/ STEMI
doses.dose: Give 4 baby aspirin chewable for a total dose of 324mg. (chewing is preferable to swallowing) give within minutes of arrival and recognition of ACS.

field.action: Anticholinergic that inhibits acetylcholine at the parasympathetic neuroeffector junction; Increases heart rate in symptomatic bradyarrhythmias; reverses muscarinic effects or cholinergic poisoning.
field.indications: Hemodynamically unstable bradycardia, organophosphate poisoning or nerve agent exposure, beta blocker or calcium channel blocker overdose.
field.contraindications: Hypersensitivity, tachydysrhythmias, hypothermic bradycardia, Acute MI, second degree, type 2 or third degree heart blocks.
field.adverse: Drowsiness, confusion, headache, palpitations, dysrythmias, nausea, vomiting, pupil dilation, dry mouth/nose/skin, blurred vision, urinary retention, constipation, flushed/dry/hot skin
field.supplied: 0.1mg/ml total of 10ml to equal 1mg of atropine in a preload, multi dose vial 20 ml with .4mg/ml to a total of 8 mg.

doses.label: Unstable Bradycardia
doses.dose: 1mg IV/IO every three to five minutes as needed, up to a total of 3mg

doses.label: Organophosphate poisoning
doses.dose: 2-4mg IV/IO repeated every 3-5 minutes until blood pressure and heart rate are stable

doses.label: Beta Blocker/Ca Channel OD
doses.dose: 1mg IV/IO every five minutes to a maximum of 3mg.

doses.label: Bradycardia
doses.dose: Give 0.02 mg/kg IV/IO up to 0.5mg (minimum dose 0.1mg). May be repeated once in 5 minutes.

doses.label: Organophosphate poisoning
doses.dose: 0.05 mg/kg IV/IO initial dose. Repeat by doubling the dose every 5 minutes until symptoms improve with age appropriate vital signs.

field.classification: Anticholinergic, bronchodilator, short acting antimuscarinic agent.
field.action: Antagonizes interaction of acetylcholine at receptors on bronchial smooth muscle, resulting in bronchodilation.
field.indications: Persistent bronchospasm, COPD exacerbation, toxic inhalation (in conjunction with Albuterol)
field.contraindications: Hypersensitivity to Atrovent, atropine and its derivatives, and those with a history of hypersensitivity to soy lecithin or related food products such as soybeans and peanuts.
field.adverse: Dizziness, headache, nervousness, palpitations, tremor, dyspnea, worsening COPD symptoms, hypertension, tachycardia, flushing, MI, dry mouth, nausea, vomiting, GI distress.
field.precautions: Used cautiously in patients with angle-closure glaucoma, prostatic hyperplasia, and bladder-neck obstruction. Avoid leakage around the face mask, temporary blurring of vision or eye pain may occur.

doses.label: Bronchospams
doses.dose: One unit dose vial (0.5mg) added to the nebulized albuterol (2.5 mg). May repeat x1.

field.action: Blocks cellular histamine1 receptors in the respiratory tract, blood vessels and GI smooth muscle; Prevents, but does not reverse, histamine-mediated responses. Reverses extrapyramidal reactions from medications doses that result in dystonic reactions.
field.contraindications: Hypersensitivity to the drug, newborns, premature neonates, or breastfeeding women (causes severe adverse effects in newborns).
field.adverse: Drowsiness, sedation, seizures, dizziness, headache, blurred vision, wheezing, thickening of bronchial secretions, palpitations, hypotension, dysrhythmias, dry mouth, diarrhea, nausea, vomiting. Hallucinations, confusion and paradoxical CNS excitation can occur in children.
field.precautions: Use with caution in asthma or COPD, increased intraocular pressure, hyperthyroidism, CV disease, hypertension, Avoid SC or perivascular injection. Drug and Alcohol use causes increased CNS depression.

doses.label: Allergic Reaction (Hives,edema), Dystonic Reaction
doses.dose: 50mg IV,IM.

doses.label: Antiemetic
doses.dose: 12.5-25mg IV/IM

doses.label: Allergic Reaction (Hives, edema), Dystonic Reaction
doses.dose: 1mg/kg IV, IM. Max of adult dose

field.classification: Sympathomimetic (sympathetic nervous system stimulator), Cardiac stimulant, bronchodilator and vasopressor (constricts blood vessels)
field.action: Stimulates alpha and beta-adrenergic receptors within the sympathetic nervous system. A potent cardiac stimulant, it strengthens the myocardial contraction (positive inotropic effect) and increases cardiac rate (positive chronotropic effect), as well as relaxes bronchial smooth muscle. Increases myocardial and cerebral blood flow during CPR.; Epinephrine strengthens the heart to contract harder and faster. Vasoconstriction effect that causes more blood flow during CPR for the heart and brain.
field.indications: Cardiac arrest, Anaphylaxis, Asthma (COPD), Beta Blocker OD, ROSC with hypotension (post fluids), Calcium Channel Blocker OD, Bradycardia unresponsive to Atropine/Pacing, Cardiogenic shock with Pulmonary Edema, Shock, Stridor caused by disease process (croup, epiglottitis, burns).
field.contraindications: Known hypersensitivity, coronary insufficiency (trauma), Relative contraindication: labor and delivery
field.adverse: Nervousness, restlessness, headache, tremor, dysrhythmias, chest pain, increased myocardial oxygen demand, hypertension, palpitations, nausea, vomiting.
field.supplied: Prefilled syringe 0.1mg/ml (1:10,000), total of 10cc = 1 mg.; (1:1,000) : Vials or ampules, multiple different variations of quantity but; always a concentration of 1 mg/ml
field.precautions: Raising blood pressure and increasing heart rate may cause myocardial ischemia, angina and increased myocardial oxygen demand. Higher doses may be required to treat poison/drug-induced shock. The effects of the drug may be potentiated by tricyclic antidepressants.; CSUS Paramedic Program Drug Sheets

doses.label: Cardiac Arrest
doses.dose: 1 mg (10 ml of 1:10,000 solution) administered every 3-5 minutes IV/IO during resuscitation. Tracheal route: 2 mg. diluted in 10ml saline.

doses.label: Anaphylaxis
doses.dose: 0.3 mg (1:1000) IM, can repeat every 5-15 minutes if effective. If no result with IM EPI and patient is hypotensive (aka shock): Push Dose Epi 5-20mcg (1:100,000) IV/IO every 2-5 min until systolic B/P > 90 mmHg

doses.label: Symptomatic Bradycardia, Beta Blocker/Calcium Channel Blocker OD, Cardiogenic & Septic shock
doses.dose: Push Dose Epi 5-20mcg (1:100,000) IV/IO every 2-5 min until systolic B/P > 90 mmHg

doses.label: Cardiac arrest
doses.dose: Give 0.01mg/kg 1:10,000 IV/IO up to a max single dose of 1mg every 3-5 minutes

doses.label: Anaphylaxis Asthma/Bronchospasm
doses.dose: 0.01 mg/kg 1:1,000 SQ or IM up to a single dose max of 0.3mg

doses.label: Symptomatic Bradycardia/ OD causing bradycardia
doses.dose: 0.01mg/kg 1:10,000 IV/IO q 3-5 min

doses.label: ROSC with unresolved shock
doses.dose: Push Dose Epi 5-20mcg 1:100,000 IV/IO every 2-5 min, until blood pressure stabilizes or 0.3mg total has been given.

doses.label: Stridor caused by disease
doses.dose: 0.5 mg 1:1000 mixed in 2ml Normal Saline and nebulized at 8 lpm O2.

field.action: Binds to opiate receptors in the CNS, producing analgesia, euphoria, respiratory depression, and sedation.
field.indications: Pain management. Alternate to NTG in patients who are positive for PED-5 administration, chest pain without pain relief after 3 NTG
field.contraindications: Hypersensitivity, use in caution with TBI, Hypotension, hypoxia, internal hemorrhage, signs of shock
field.adverse: Confusion, blurred vision, apnea, laryngospasm, allergic reaction, respiratory depression, arrhythmias, hypotension, nausea, vomiting, skeletal and thoracic muscle rigidity
field.precautions: Chest wall rigidity possible with a high dose rapid push.

doses.label: Suspected cardiac chest discomfort/ STEMI
doses.dose: Post 3 Nitro or if Nitro is contraindicated, give 1mcg/kg IV, IO, IM, IN slow push. Can consider repeating once after 5 minutes for total of 2mcg/kg if pain has not been managed. Max single dose 100mcg

doses.label: Burns
doses.dose: 1mcg/kg IV, IM, IO slow push. Can consider repeating twice after 5 minutes for total of 3mcg/kg if pain has not been managed. Max single dose 100mcg.

doses.label: Trauma
doses.dose: 1mcg/kg IV, IM, IO slow push. Can consider repeating once after 5 minutes for total of 2mcg/kg if pain has not been managed. Max single dose 100mcg.

doses.label: Other
doses.dose: 1mcg/kg IV, IM, IO slow push. Can consider repeating once after 5 minutes for total of 2mcg/kg if pain has not been managed. Max single dose 100mcg.

field.action: Cardiac: Combines with fast sodium channels, thereby inhibiting recovery after repolarization, and decreasing myocardial excitability and conduction velocity.; Local Anesthetic: inhibits ion transport across the neuronal membrane, blocking conduction of normal nerve impulses.
field.indications: Cardiac arrest from VF/VT , Stable pulsing VT (Amiodarone is preferred). Alternative to Amiodarone. Prevents a rise in intracranial pressure associated with administration of succinylcholine and the intubation procedure, conscious IO.
field.contraindications: Hypersensitivity to the drug, 2nd or 3rd Degree heart blocks, Stokes-Adams syndrome (sudden, brief loss of consciousness from a large drop in cardiac output), Wide complex escape beats with bradycardia.
field.adverse: Drowsiness, confusion, seizures, slurred speech, hypotension, dysrhythmias, cardiac arrest, nausea, vomiting.

doses.label: VF/ Pulseless VT Perfusing stable wide complex tachycardia
doses.dose: 1-1.5 mg/kg IV/IO repeated every 5 min at half doses of original dose (0.5-0.75mg/kg) to a max of 3 mg/kg total dosage maintenance infusion at 1 to 4 mg per minute IV/IO

doses.label: Pain management in a conscious IO
doses.dose: 0.5mg/kg (max of 40mg) (2% Lidocaine) IO slowly over 1-2 minutes, flush with 10mL normal saline after one minute.

doses.label: VF, pulsless VT, wide tachycardia(with pulses)
doses.dose: 1mg/kg IV/IO (max 100mg)

doses.label: Pain management in a conscious IO
doses.dose: 0.5mg/kg (max of 20mg) IO slowly over 1-2 minutes, followed by 10ml flush normal saline after one minute.

field.action: Primary effects is vasodilation of coronary and cerebral arteries, which causes the following.; Increase in coronary blood flow; Decreased work load/myocardial oxygen demand; Decreased peripheral resistance (afterload); Reduce venous tone; causes blood pooling in peripheral veins, decreasing venous return to the heart (preload); Dilation of coronary arteries (if not already at max)and relief of coronary artery spasm.; Generalized smooth muscle relaxant
field.indications: Angina; Chest pain suggestive of a MI; Pulmonary edema
field.contraindications: Hypotension; Chest trauma; Cerebral bleeding; Head trauma; Increased ICP; Use of sexually enhancing drugs (Viagra, Cilailis, Sildenafil, tadalafil, vardenafil ) within previous 24; Hypersensitivity; Strongly suspected Inferior/RV infarction from 12lead EKG
field.adverse: Headache, transient episodes of light-headedness related to blood pressure changes, hypotension, syncope, crescendo angina, rebound hypertension
field.supplied: Pumpspray 400 mcg per spray, (200 metered sprays). Tablets 0.4mg S.L. Paste of 2% with measuring applicators for transdermal use (1inch =1g)
field.precautions: Do not shake aerosol spray container because this affects metered dose. Patient should sit or lie down when taking this drug. Concomitant use of nitrates and alcohol may cause hypotension. Marked symptomatic orthostatic hypotension may occur when calcium channel blockers and oral controlled-release nitroglycerin are used in combination.

doses.label: Cardiac related chest discomfort/ STEMI
doses.dose: 0.4 mg (gr. 1/150) tablet or one metered spray (400mcg) SL May repeat same dosage for chest discomfort every 5 minutes to a max of 3 doses if SBP remains 90 or greater. If discomfort dissipates prior to giving 3 doses, do not give any more. If pain remains after 3 nitro doses, consider fentanyl or morphine.

doses.label: CHF with Pulmonary Edema
doses.dose: Titrate Dose based on SBP. Administer prior to applying CPAP if possible: SBP > 200 : 1.2mg SL SBP 151-200 : 0.8mg SL SBP 100-150 :0.4mg SL Post applying CPAP, you want to utilize Nitro paste as the alternative. Do not remove CPAP if you do not have to and it is working properly. 1-2 inches (1-2g) on the chest wall

field.action: Stimulates smooth muscle receptors, potent vasoconstrictor
field.indications: Alternative for the treatment of shock-refractory VF, asystole or PEA. May be substituted for epinephrine as an alternative agent as a single one time dose.
field.contraindications: Use with caution in patients with CAD, epilepsy or heart failure
field.adverse: Headache, seizure, bronchospasm, anaphylaxis, angina, arrhythmias, myocardial ischemia, decreased cardiac output, abdominal cramps, nausea and vomiting.

doses.label: Cardiac Arrest
doses.dose: 40 Units(U) IV/IO push in place of the first or second dose of epi in cardiac arrest
